newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss government wants talks on Holocaust fund.
newsitem.headline: Swiss government wants talks on Holocaust fund.

text.p: The Swiss government said on Tuesday it wanted immediate talks with banks and Jewish groups on using dormant Swiss accounts, some left by victims of Nazi persecution, to create a Holocaust memorial fund.

The Federal Council, the Swiss cabinet, also criticised threats by Jewish groups to call a boycott of Swiss banks as endangering joint efforts to track Jewish wealth and Nazi loot sent to neutral Switzerland before and during World War Two.
The seven-member Federal Council also refused to apologise for comments by Economics Minister Jean-Pascal Delamuraz that Jewish calls for a Swiss Holocaust memorial fund were "blackmail".

A statement after the ministers conferred by telephone said the government wanted dormant bank accounts, which a search has so far found to total 40 million Swiss francs ($30 million), be "put to a proper use".

"In this respect, the Federal Council is ready to immediately take up discussions with the banks and the interested organisations regarding the creation of a fund in favour of Holocaust victims and their descendants," the statement said.
A government official said Berne had already contacted Swiss banks and expected to decide by the end of January whether to create a fund with the dormant accounts. ($1=1.3555 Swiss Franc)
